text:
emma-support: FYI merchant reports a spike of card declines on invoices for UK customers after PO workflow change. customer sees AVS/CVV failures.
merchant-cs: Yep, just got an angry message from Acme Ltd — multiple retries, all declined. They attached one declined txn id 9876543210.
payments-bot: Charge 9876543210: decline_code=avs_reject, cvv_check=fail, issuer_response=Cardholder verification failed
sam-payments: Thanks — can you paste the invoiced billing address (as captured in our request) and the cardholder-provided address? Need to check normalization.
merchant-cs: Billing address in system: "Flat 2, 18 Oldham Rd, Manchester, M4 1AB, UK". Cardholder entered: "2 Flat, Oldham Road, Manchester M4 1AB". PO number on file: PO-7788.
li-reliability: Hmm looks like address line order is flipped. Our AVS matcher uses normalized ordering + postcode. UK AVS is noisy though. Can you share raw request body from the failing attempts?
dmitri-ops: Repro step I used in staging: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/payments -d '{"amount":12000,"card":{"number":"4000000000003220","exp":"12/26","cvc":"123"},"billing":{"line1":"2 Flat","line2":"Oldham Road","city":"Manchester","postcode":"M4 1AB"}}' and got same avs_reject.
emma-support: That test card (4000...3220) is our AVS-failure simulator — good repro. Merchant says real customers are using valid cards.
sam-payments: Quick note: Issuer returns avs_code=X and cvv_code=N for the declines. X usually means unmatched address. CVV N indicates incorrect CVC — but in some networks CVV set to N if AVS fails upstream.
merchant-cs: Is there a short-term workaround? Clients need to pay today to fulfill POs.
li-reliability: Two ideas: 1) Relax strict AVS rejection for legacy PO invoices — allow manual review path; 2) Normalization tweak: accept swapped line1/line2 if postcode & city match.
dmitri-ops: I can push a feature-flagged change to normalization to attempt line swap match. Will need a quick canary on a subset of traffic. ETA 2 hours if approved.
sam-payments: Before changing flow, confirm fraud risk. If we relax AVS, need a compensating rule: require successful 3DS or verification from gateway. Do we have 3DS enabled for these merchants?
merchant-cs: Acme is not on 3DS yet — they are B2B with PO terms. They specifically asked to bypass extra friction.
emma-support: For immediate relief, can payments team perform a manual retry through processor with AVS override? Sometimes processors allow force-accept for enterprise merchants.
sam-payments: I'll check with our acquirer rep. If they allow override, we'll need merchant sign-off and a temporary ledger flag. Pinged acquirer: acquirer@example.com
payments-bot: Acquirer reply: "We can process AVS override for PO merchants on case-by-case basis. Provide txn ids and signed merchant waiver."
dmitri-ops: OK, I'll assemble a minimal script to bulk-retry a list of txn ids via gateway sandbox—will require merchant's signed waiver stored on support ticket.
li-reliability: Parallel track: I'll prepare a normalization patch (swap line1/line2) behind feature flag + metric to track fraud/chargeback rate. roll out to 5% traffic.
sam-payments: Sounds good. For longer term: add a PO field in invoice schema that sets a lower AVS strictness profile when present and merchant has enterprise risk profile validated.
emma-support: Action items: 1) merchant-cs obtain signed waiver (merchant), 2) sam to confirm acquirer override and provide steps, 3) dmitri to run bulk-retry if override approved, 4) li to implement feature-flagged normalization and monitor metrics.
merchant-cs: I'll email the merchant and drop the signed waiver into the ticket within 90 minutes.
sam-payments: Acquirer confirmed they can accept override. Need the signed waiver and list of txn ids. Also need last4, amount, and timestamp for PCI compliance.
dmitri-ops: I'll prepare a CSV template: txn_id,last4,amount_cents,ts and a one-liner script to call the gateway. Will wait for waiver before running.
li-reliability: Deploy plan for normalization: dev -> staging smoke (address-swap tests) -> canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%. If fraud signals spike, rollback immediately.
emma-support: I'll coordinate comms with the merchant and keep this thread updated. Thanks all :thumbsup:
merchant-cs: Merchant confirmed PO urgency, sending waiver now.
sam-payments: Received waiver PDF. Can you also confirm the list of affected txn ids (they provided 6 ids). Forwarding to acquirer.
dmitri-ops: Running bulk-retry now (dry-run first) against gateway sandbox. Logs:
```
[2025-09-12T14:22:01Z] retry_txn 9876543210 -> result=accepted_override code=00
[2025-09-12T14:22:02Z] retry_txn 9876543211 -> result=accepted_override code=00
```
payments-bot: Production retry queued for 6 txns; operator=dmitri-ops; hold_until=manual_confirm
emma-support: Approved, proceed to production retry. Please report completion and settle invoices.
dmitri-ops: Production retries done. 6 of 6 accepted. Merchant notified and invoices marked paid.
merchant-cs: Confirmed customer payments received and PO fulfilled. Thanks team!
li-reliability: I'll still proceed with the normalization feature flag rollout tomorrow to prevent recurrence.
emma-support: Closing loop. Saved postmortem notes in ticket #4521 and assigned follow-ups to product/payments.
sam-payments: Adding a follow-up to product: add PO-based AVS profile + 3DS opt-in for enterprise flows.
emma-support: Great. Thread closed.
